author: zx123
text_post: Hi, I have been love shy for as long as I can remember. I suppose I always wanted a relationship, but I sort of excepted that I couldn't have one. Now that I am older I have started feel more restricted by my inability to have a relationship, as a result of which I have become increasingly preoccupied with finding a solution. Basically, I need to know if there is any realistic possibility of changing from being love shy and what I need to do to achieve it. Do I need to go to bars or clubs and talk to women?, something which would be difficult for me as I am extremely shy. Do I need to be more social and try to gain a wider social circle?,  Could some sort of therapy such as exposure therapy work? Could meeting other people who are also love shy help? I need to know what I need to do so that I can at least try. In addition, please could somebody answer these questions about love shyness? Is there any realistic hope of changing from being love shy to being able to have relationships? Has anyone ever been able to recover from love shyness and start having relationship? Could somebody post some examples of people who have recovered from love shyness? Thank you,

author: ieatboogers
text_post: Yes, it can be defeated. Several people who post here have done it.  There are several methods you can try, but the best one for you will depend on your personality and individual circumstances.  Take a look at the sticky threads in the "Recovery" forum and start there.

author: Someone
text_post: I speculate that exposure therapy might be one of the best solitions. Humans adjust, that is their strength. I don't think that you can fully overcome love-shyness as a trait of your personality, but you might be able to counter how it affects your everyday life by practising and practising, adjusting yourself to the exposure, getting used to the awkwardness of such situations and thereby slowly taking the tension out of them.  I guess it's more or less a treatment of the symptoms, not of the condition itself. However, if that is what you seek, I figure that this might be the best way to go. You gotta have thick skin though, rejection and awkwardness will take their toll, it will be rough. But as I said, it's just speculation, I never got out of this by overcoming it, but by quitting.

author: Rudeboy41
text_post: Bars and clubs.  Funny thing, I was in a club a couple of weeks ago on business.  Unfortunately the answer is no.  Clubs are there to sell alcohol.  If people were successful at socialising in clubs, no alcohol would be sold.  Clubs feed upon the social inadequacy of their customers.  Stressed out people buy booze.  Happy people buy nothing.  People at bars and clubs are in a state of hysteria, and their defences are all the way up.  Clubs are not places to relax, nor are they socialy conducive. Quote:Do I need to be more social and try to gain a wider social circle?,  Not really.  When people try to be more social, it backfires.  There is nothing more iritating than people trying to be social.  You can't be more social than you already are.  Humans are hard wired to be social. Therefore you cannot not be social.  A pain in the arse is sociality gone wrong.  You will only meet people you don't want in your life. Quote: Could some sort of therapy such as exposure therapy work? Hmmm, no.  There is a fairly dark secret in this world.  Just go for a walk in a busy city.  Most of the people you see look beaten down, and not the sort of people you'd want to waste your time on, with homeless people being at the bottom of the pile.  The dark secret is that many people see you as inadequate and someone they do not want in their lives.  You don't know what it is that would make them like you, and they will never tell you in such a way that you could put the knowledge to practical use.  In short, exposure does not expose. Quote:Could meeting other people who are also love shy help? You probably have already met too many love shy people already.  They are not terribly inspiring.  It's like a tramp meeting another tramp.  Does it help the tramp to meet other tramps? Quote: I need to know what I need to do so that I can at least try. There isn't really anything to try.  To try is to be an addict.  Only addicts try.  A heroin addict tries to be free from heroin by taking more heroin.  A battered wife tries by finding husbands to batter her.  If you want to be even more love shy, then trying anything will probably work. Quote: In addition, please could somebody answer these questions about love shyness? Is there any realistic hope of changing from being love shy to being able to have relationships? Yes, but not the one you're after Quote:Has anyone ever been able to recover from love shyness and start having relationship? Yes Quote:Could somebody post some examples of people who have recovered from love shyness? Thank you, Just go on youtube.  Any success story will do.  Something wih the title "How I went from being shy and single, to finding love and confidence."

author: zx123
text_post: Hi,  thinks for your replies?! Well, since I posted that I have been doing some research and I think I may have found the answer, or at least an answer to recover from love shyness. I now believe the answer to love shyness could be held in the form of some sort of exposure therapy. It makes sense, surely if you are love shy the one thing you have avoided has been to interact with members f the opposite sex, especially particularly attractive ones. As such, the love shy person has become the subject of a problem which is underpinned by a lack of experiences thereby causing them to feel a lack of self belief in their abilities. It holds true for many different things aside from love shyness that if you put yourself in that situation so many time, you will become acclimatised to it. Human beings can change, so if you have learnt to be love shy surely it must be possible to learnt not to be love shy. People are not born love shy, it is a learnt behaviour. An example of what I am talking about can be seen in this thread, where the went out of his comfort zone to confront what he feared, talking to women. I am not claiming this as the definitive solution to love shyness, but at the moment it is the best idea that I can find. viewtopic.php?f=3&t=12024
